stories.headline: TSMC Q1 Revenue Surges 35% YoY to $35.7B, Beating Estimates as AI Chip Demand Holds

key_facts.fact: TSMC reported Q1 2026 revenue of T$1.134 trillion ($35.71 billion), up 35% year-over-year from T$839.3 billion in Q1 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: January-March revenue reached T$1.134 trillion ($35.71 billion) compared with T$839.3 billion in the same period a year earlier, TSMC said in a statement.

key_facts.fact: The result beat the LSEG SmartEstimate of T$1.125 trillion drawn from 20 analysts, and was in line with TSMC's own January guidance of $34.6B to $35.8B.
key_facts.excerpt: The result topped an LSEG SmartEstimate of T$1.125 trillion drawn from 20 analysts, and was in line with TSMC's January guidance of $34.6 billion to $35.8 billion.

key_facts.fact: Analysts raised their forecast for TSMC's Q2 revenue by 2.3% over the last 30 days to a record T$1.2 trillion, betting on constrained capacity for advanced AI chip production.
key_facts.excerpt: Analysts nevertheless raised their forecast for TSMC's April-June revenue by 2.3 per cent over the last 30 days to a record T$1.2 trillion.

key_facts.fact: TSMC's 2nm (N2) node capacity is fully booked for 2026 with Apple and Nvidia securing the bulk of early output; capacity is planned to double by 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: N2 capacity, which is already fully booked for 2026 with Apple and Nvidia securing the bulk of early output, is planned to double by 2027.

key_facts.fact: TSMC raised its 2026 capital expenditure budget to $52B–$56B, roughly 30% above the $40.9B spent in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC has aggressively raised its capital expenditure budget for 2026 to a range of $52 billion to $56 billion, a roughly 30% increase from the $40.9 billion spent the previous year.

key_facts.fact: TSMC will report full Q1 earnings and an updated outlook for Q2 and the full year on April 16.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC will report first-quarter earnings on April 16 along with an updated outlook for the current quarter and full year.

stories.headline: RISC-V Chip Designer SiFive Raises $400M Series G at $3.65B Valuation, Eyes IPO

key_facts.fact: SiFive raised $400 million in an oversubscribed Series G round led by Atreides Management, with participation from Apollo, Nvidia, Point72 Turion, and T. Rowe Price.
key_facts.excerpt: This equity funding round was led by Atreides Management with other A-list investors including Apollo Global Management, NVIDIA, Point72 Turion, and T. Rowe Price Investment Management.

key_facts.fact: The financing values SiFive at $3.65 billion and CEO Patrick Little said he expects it to be the firm's last private round before filing for a public offering.
key_facts.excerpt: The round brings SiFive's valuation to $3.65 billion, and CEO Patrick Little told Reuters he expects it to be the firm's last round of funding before filing for a public offering.

key_facts.fact: SiFive sells customizable RISC-V processor IP — not chips — that customers like Google can use for their own internal chip designs, competing with Arm Holdings.
key_facts.excerpt: SiFive does not sell chips but instead sells blueprints that customers such as Alphabet's Google can customize for their own internal chip designs.

key_facts.fact: Arm's recent move to develop its own chips created an opening for SiFive, as Arm became a potential competitor to its longtime customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Arm last month unveiled its own chips, making Arm for the first time a potential competitor to many of its longtime customers.

key_facts.fact: SiFive will use the funding to develop a data center CPU design and expand global engineering teams, with existing ports of CUDA, RedHat, and Ubuntu on its platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Accelerate data center software development on the SiFive platform, building on existing ports of CUDA, RedHat and Ubuntu.

sources.title: SiFive Raises $400 Million to Accelerate High-Performance RISC-V Data Center Solutions
SiFive raises $400 million from Atreides, Nvidia for data-center chip technology

stories.headline: Amazon's Custom Chip Business Hits $20B+ Run Rate; Jassy Floats Selling Chips to Third Parties

key_facts.fact: Amazon's custom chip business — Graviton CPUs, Trainium AI chips, and Nitro networking cards — now has an annualized revenue run rate of over $20 billion, doubling from $10B disclosed with Q4 results.
key_facts.excerpt: That business, which includes Graviton processors, Trainium AI chips and Nitro networking cards, now has an annualized revenue run-rate of over $20 billion, doubling from the $10 billion disclosed alongside fourth-quarter results.

key_facts.fact: Jassy said if the chip unit operated as a standalone business selling to third parties, it could achieve an annual run rate of around $50 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Selling to AWS and external customers alike, as standalone chipmakers do, would put annual revenue at around $50 billion, up from the $20 billion the company estimates for the year, Jassy said.

key_facts.fact: Jassy wrote 'There's so much demand for our chips that it's quite possible we'll sell racks of them to third parties in the future.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'There's so much demand for our chips that it's quite possible we'll sell racks of them to third parties in the future,' Jassy wrote in his annual shareholder letter.

key_facts.fact: AWS's AI business is running at over $15 billion in annualized revenue as of Q1 2026, the first time Amazon has reported the figure.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon's AI services at its cloud-computing unit are generating annualized revenue of more than $15 billion, CEO Andy Jassy said, the first time the company has reported numbers on a business it has backed with billions of dollars in investment.

key_facts.fact: Trainium2 is fully allocated, Trainium3 (reaching customers early 2026) has nearly all supply reserved, and Trainium4 already has substantial pre-orders.
key_facts.excerpt: Trainium2 is essentially unavailable, with its entire allocated capacity spoken for. Trainium3 started reaching customers in early 2026, and reservations have filled nearly all available supply. Even Trainium4 — which is not expected to reach wide release for another year and a half — has substantial pre-orders.

key_facts.fact: Amazon projects roughly $200 billion in capital expenditure in 2026, mainly focused on AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: The company projected $200 billion in capital expenditure this year, mainly focused on AI, a figure that spooked investors and fanned worries about an industry bubble.

key_facts.fact: Jassy said using Trainium at scale would 'save tens of billions of capex dollars per year, and provide several hundred basis points of operating margin advantage versus relying on others' chips.'
key_facts.excerpt: He estimated that by using its own Trainium chips at scale, the company will 'save tens of billions of capex dollars per year, and provide several hundred basis points of operating margin advantage versus relying on others' chips for inference.'

stories.headline: Anthropic Weighs Designing Its Own AI Chips as Revenue Surpasses $30B Annualized

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is exploring the possibility of designing its own chips, according to three sources, though plans are in preliminary stages and the company could still opt to only purchase chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is weighing the possibility of designing its own AI chips… The plans are in preliminary stages, and the company could still opt to only purchase AI chips and not design any.

key_facts.fact: The company has yet to commit to a specific design or assemble a dedicated team for chip development.
key_facts.excerpt: The company may ultimately choose to rely solely on purchasing AI chips rather than developing its own, as it has yet to commit to a specific design or assemble a dedicated team for the effort.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic currently trains and runs Claude using a mix of AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and Nvidia GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said it trains and runs Claude using a mix of AI hardware, including Trainium from Amazon Web Services, Google TPUs, and NVIDIA GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's annualized revenue now exceeds $30 billion, up from around $9 billion at the end of 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's annualized revenue now exceeding $30 billion, up from around $9 billion at the end of 2025.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom has signed a deal to provide Anthropic with access to around 3.5 gigawatts of AI computing capacity using Google's processors starting in 2027.

stories.headline: Google and Intel Expand Multiyear Deal on Xeon CPUs and Custom ASIC-Based IPUs for AI

key_facts.fact: Intel and Google announced a multiyear collaboration to deploy multiple generations of Intel Xeon processors (including Xeon 6) across Google Cloud and to co-develop next-generation custom ASIC-based IPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: As part of the multiyear agreement, announced Thursday, the search engine giant will customize Intel's IPUs, or infrastructure processing units.

key_facts.fact: Intel's custom ASIC business grew more than 50% in 2025 and exited Q4 at an annualized revenue run rate above $1 billion, per Intel CFO David Zinsner.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel CFO David Zinsner had alluded to increased demand for these services during the company's Q4 earnings call in January, touting that the company's custom ASIC biz grew more than 50 percent in 2025 and exited Q4 at an annualized revenue run rate above $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: The IPUs offload networking, security, and storage operations from host CPUs, freeing resources for AI tenant workloads — similar in concept to Amazon's Nitro NICs and Microsoft's FPGA-based approach.
key_facts.excerpt: These devices are essentially a computer on a network card and are designed to offload networking, security, and storage operations, freeing up CPU resources for tenant workloads.

key_facts.fact: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated: 'Scaling AI requires more than accelerators — it requires balanced systems.'
key_facts.excerpt: Getting a bigger slice of data center spending is critical to a comeback bid under Chief Executive Officer Lip-Bu Tan.

key_facts.fact: Google's Amin Vahdat, SVP and Chief Technologist of AI Infrastructure, called Intel a 'trusted partner for nearly two decades' and said its Xeon road map gives confidence to meet growing AI demands.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Intel has been a trusted partner for nearly two decades, and their Xeon road map gives us confidence that we can continue to meet the growing performance and efficiency demands of our workloads.'

stories.headline: Chinese AI Firm Sharetronic Disclosed $92M in Banned Nvidia Chip Servers After Super Micro Charges

key_facts.fact: Shenzhen-based Sharetronic Data Technology's stock plunged 20% (daily limit) hours after the US charged Super Micro Computer co-founder with smuggling billions in Nvidia chips to China.
key_facts.excerpt: Hours after the United States charged a Super Micro Computer (SMCI) co-founder with illegally smuggling billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia (NVDA) AI chips to China, shares of a little-known Shenzhen-based computing company plummeted by the daily limit of 20%.

key_facts.fact: Records filed with Chinese government agencies show Sharetronic procured hundreds of Super Micro systems containing banned Nvidia H100 and H200 chips worth approximately $92 million (6.32 billion yuan).
key_facts.excerpt: Two invoices from May and June — documenting sales from Sharetronic to a subsidiary — named 276 Super Micro systems that use Nvidia H100 and H200 chips, plus a smaller batch of 32 Dell products dubbed the PowerEdge XE9680.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg found 17 invoices in China's national tax database totaling approximately 60 billion yuan, representing only about one-fifth of Sharetronic's planned total procurement.
key_facts.excerpt: 彭博記者透過比對發票號碼、日期與總金額，在中國國家稅務總局資料庫中找到 17 份完整發票，累計總值約 60 億人民幣，僅佔 Sharetronic 計劃採購總量的五分之一。

key_facts.fact: Sharetronic's subsidiary FCloud, established in 2024, became one of only 8 certified Nvidia Cloud Partners in China and announced plans to procure 32.2 billion yuan in hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: FCloud 於 2024 年甫成立，卻在年末取得 Nvidia 雲端合作夥伴（NCP）資質，成為全中國僅有的 8 家認證夥伴之一。FCloud 同年宣布計劃採購總值高達 322 億人民幣的硬體裝置。

key_facts.fact: Nvidia, Super Micro, and Dell all denied having sales relationships with Sharetronic, which also denied any business cooperation with Super Micro — contradicting the invoice records.
key_facts.excerpt: Records filed with Chinese government agencies suggest Sharetronic procured hundreds of Super Micro systems containing high-end Nvidia chips, which have been banned from unauthorized sale to and within China.

key_facts.fact: Super Micro co-founder was charged by the DOJ with helping transfer approximately $2.5 billion in Nvidia servers to China; smuggling methods included forged export documents and shell servers in warehouses.
key_facts.excerpt: 超微電腦共同創辦人廖義賢於 2026 年 3 月遭美國司法部起訴，指控其協助將價值約 25 億美元的 Nvidia 伺服器非法轉運至中國…走私手法包括偽造出口檔案、將伺服器重新包裝，以及在倉庫中放置空殼伺服器以規避查驗。

stories.headline: Unitree to Launch $4,370 Humanoid Robot R1 Globally via AliExpress Next Week

key_facts.fact: Unitree Robotics will launch its cheapest humanoid robot, the R1, in international markets next week via Alibaba's AliExpress platform, according to two sources familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: Unitree Robotics will launch its cheapest humanoid robot model, R1, in international markets next week via AliExpress, a global e-commerce platform under Alibaba Group.

key_facts.fact: The R1 is priced at 29,900 yuan (~$4,370) in China, making it one of the most affordable humanoid robots on the market. Overseas pricing has not been announced.
key_facts.excerpt: R1, which was launched in mainland China last year, is currently the most affordable humanoid robot offered by Unitree Robotics, with prices starting at 29,900 yuan (approximately $4,370).

key_facts.fact: The launch will cover North America, Europe, Japan, and Singapore, with additional channels to follow later.
key_facts.excerpt: The release will cover major overseas markets including North America, Europe, Japan, and Singapore. The second source indicated that the product will later be made available through other channels.

key_facts.fact: The R1 stands 123cm tall, weighs at least 27kg, has 26 joints, and can perform cartwheels, run downhill, lie down and stand up unassisted.
key_facts.excerpt: It stands about 1.2 meters tall and weighs roughly 25-27 kg… It features 26 joints for flexible movement and is powered by onboard computing capable of handling voice and image-based interactions.

key_facts.fact: The R1 will be available through Alibaba's Brand+ channel on AliExpress, the curated storefront for globally recognized brands.
key_facts.excerpt: AliExpress, especially through Alibaba's Brand+ channel, lends the R1 a passport to legitimacy in overseas markets while preserving the aura of a value proposition.
